newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's NAP plans six-party coalition govt.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's NAP plans six-party coalition govt.

text.p: Thailand's New Aspiration Party (NAP) said on Monday it had agreed to form a six-party coalition that would be the basis of the next government.

"We agreed to form a six-party coalition that would include the NAP, Chart Pattana, Social Action Party, Prachakorn Thai, Seritham and Muan Chon parties," said NAP leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh after a meeting on the formation of the coalition.
The parties signed a pact to jointly nominate Chavalit for the prime ministership, the NAP leader said in the presence of the leaders of the coalition partners.
The six-member coalition would have a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-seat parliament.

Late on Sunday, after the NAP won a two-seat victory in the election over its arch-rival the Democrat Party of former prime minister Chuan Leekpai, Chavalit appeared with leaders of four parties and said they were discussing forming a coalition.
But the group has since changed, with the new six-member coalition adding Chart Pattana and Seritham Parties.
It does not include the Chart Thai party led by caretaker prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa -- who was part of the four in talks on Sunday night. Chart Thai won 39 seats.
Some analysts said Chavalit decided to include Chart Pattana, led by charismatic former premier Chatichai Choonhavan, instead of Chart Thai to try and avoid image problems.
Chart Thai leader Banharn dissolved parliament after a bruising no-confidence debate in September. His party and the former ruling coalition were accused of mismanagement and corruption.
Banharn was forced to resign by coalition partners, led by Chavalit, after the no-confidence debate.

"The sense of mistrust still prevails between Banharn and Chavalit so I think the (coalition) would include Chart Pattana which has a better public image than Chart Thai," Ramkhamheang University political scientist Sukhum Naunsakul told reporters.
Chavalit did not say how he would distribute the portfolios. He said it would take some time to name cabinet members, but he would try to do it as soon as possible.
Earlier, he stressed it was important that his cabinet was acceptable to the public.
The stock market plunged around six percent when it opened on Monday as investors reacted to the NAP victory. By 0800 GMT, the index was down 50.53 points, or 5.05 percent, at 950.20.
The slide reversed a two-week rally that had built in anticipation of a Democrat victory.
Market analysts said the market fall was because investors felt the new government would just be a revamped version of the old coalition led by Banharn's Chart Thai party.
